title: Traveller Club Relief Against the Excess Borne on Car Rental Damage
content:
The excess a renter bears on damage to a vehicle hired under the Car Rental Rate Classes may be relieved
where a collision damage waiver was sold on that rental. What decides it is the rental's own ledger and the standing of the
renter's Wanderlane Traveller Club membership.

**Where the ledger carries a collision damage waiver sold on the rental and the renter holds an active club
membership whose tier carries a car rental discount**, the excess borne is the rate class's waiver excess
reduced by that tier's car rental discount.

**Where the ledger carries a collision damage waiver sold on the rental and the renter holds no active club
membership carrying a car rental discount**, the excess borne is the rate class's waiver excess reduced by
2 per cent.

**Where the ledger carries no collision damage waiver sold on the rental**, no reduction under this head is
made to the excess borne.

## What counts as a waiver sold on the rental

A waiver sold on the rental is a waiver standing on that rental's own ledger. A waiver carried in the rate
class rather than sold as a line is not a waiver sold on the rental, and neither of the first two rows is
reached.

The two relieved rows divide on the membership alone, and between them they cover every rental whose ledger
carries a waiver sold on it: a renter with a qualifying tier takes that tier's own discount, and every other
renter takes 2 per cent.

## Two renters compared

A rental on a class whose waiver excess is 1200 USD, whose ledger carries a collision damage waiver sold on
it, held by a renter with no active membership carrying a car rental discount: the excess borne is 1200 USD
less 2 per cent of it, which is 1176 USD. Held by a renter whose active membership stands at a tier carrying
a car rental discount of 15 per cent, the excess borne is 1200 USD less 15 per cent of it, which is 1020 USD.
